text: dsh-nested-followups（DSH 插件，Web 与官方 Desktop 客户端）：在对话中把任意已完成的助手回答变成隔离的追问分支，并可在分支内继续递归分叉。插件注册 Tree View 会话视图和标题栏切换按钮，通过宿主服务读取会话树、创建分支、继续分支并级联删除。分支从所选回答的历史边界派生，树状画布支持搜索、聚焦、缩放、折叠和小地图，分支元数据会持久保存。适合需要探索旁支问题、同时保留主对话脉络的 DSH 用户。需要兼容版本的 DeepSeek Harness；不需要额外 API Key 或外部服务。

dsh-nested-followups adds a Tree View to DSH Web and official Desktop. Create isolated follow-up branches from completed answers, nest branches, continue branches, and navigate or delete them in a tree. Requires compatible DeepSeek Harness; no API key needed.
想从某条回答旁边开个追问分支，别把主对话弄乱。
有没有办法在 DSH 里对一个回答继续追问，但保留原来的聊天记录？
我想把支线问题再分叉出去，一层套一层地探索。
让 DSH 把长对话整理成主线和可展开的旁支树。
怎么在某个分支的最新回答下面接着聊？
想在大对话里查找回答，并展开它上面的折叠分支。
我想删除一个旁支时，把它下面的子分支也一起清掉。
I want to ask a side question from an earlier answer without adding it to the main chat.
Can I branch from a reply inside a branch and keep exploring recursively?
I need a visual tree to navigate and continue separate conversation threads in DSH.
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「从回答创建追问分支」：在 Tree View 选择已完成的助手回答并提交问题，会创建一个继承该回答之前历史的新会话；该回答位于主线或现有分支时都可作为锚点。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「递归嵌套分支」：在任一分支回答上再次选择 Ask follow-up，可从该分支历史创建子分支，形成可继续扩展的会话树。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「继续当前分支」：在分支最新完成的助手回答处提交下一条问题，内容追加到当前分支会话；主对话不提供此操作。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「对话树视图」：从会话标题栏切换到 Tree View，以节点展示主线与分支，并读取树快照和更新。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「树内导航」：在对话树中搜索并展开折叠祖先，配合聚焦、平移、缩放、适配视图和小地图浏览较大的分支树。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「级联删除分支」：删除指定分支时连同其后代分支会一并标记并清理会话，界面可以展示受影响分支和消息数量。
dsh-nested-followups 的功能「保存树关系」：将树与分支记录保存在 DSH storage domain 中，使插件卸载或重启后仍可读取分支元数据。
dsh-nested-followups 使用前须知：创建或继续分支需要宿主提供兼容的 Agent、隐藏分支和工具执行限制能力；能力不可用时相关操作会被关闭。

**Branch from any answer. Keep branching at any depth.**

dsh-nested-followups README · dsh-nested-followups：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin
for isolated follow-ups that can keep branching recursively, with no
plugin-defined depth limit. Start a side trail from any answer, then turn any
answer anywhere in that trail into the next isolated fork point. Repeat for as
many levels as the question needs. Every level inherits only its ancestor path,
while the main task stays linear and untouched.

dsh-nested-followups README · dsh-nested-followups：[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-nested-followups)
[](docs/dsh-version-compatibility.md)
[](docs/dsh-version-compatibility.md)
[](LICENSE)

_Recorded in an unmodified DeepSeek Harness `0.1.1-rc.2` web profile. The UI
and sessions are real; the captions and cursor are added in post._

> **MAIN TASK → SIDE QUESTION → NESTED SIDE QUESTION → NEST AGAIN → …**

dsh-nested-followups README · dsh-nested-followups：- **Start a side trail anywhere.** The first branch receives exactly the history
  that existed at the selected answer.
- **Keep branching at any depth.** Every answer in every side trail can become
  another isolated fork point. Apply the same action again at every new level.
- **Keep the main task clean.** Nothing asked or answered in a branch flows back
  into the main conversation.

dsh-nested-followups README · Install：Choose the install path that matches your DeepSeek Harness line:

| DeepSeek Harness | Plugin source | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0.1.0-rc.7` through `0.1.1-rc.2` | npm `dsh-nested-followups@0.2.3` | Legacy host support retained |
| `0.2.1-rc.5` Web / official Desktop | npm `dsh-nested-followups@0.2.3` | Current development target |
| `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.2-alpha.2` | Same package | Additional verified preview targets |

dsh-nested-followups README · Install：**DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`: use the exact plugin version below.** If Plugin Hub reports
that `dsh-nested-followups@0.2.2` is incompatible, it installed the old artifact,
even if its command said `@latest`. A fresh rc.5 profile reproduced that fallback
after `0.2.3` was published; explicitly requesting `@0.2.3` installs successfully.
pnpm 11's default [one-day release-age window](https://pnpm.io/blog/releases/11.0#security--build-defaults)
can cause this immediately after a release. Do not grant a compatibility
exemption to `0.2.2` or disable the profile's release-age protection.

dsh-nested-followups README · Web：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-nested-followups@0.2.3
```

Restart the DeepSeek Harness web profile if it is already running, open a
conversation, and select **Tree View**.

dsh-nested-followups README · Build from source (optional, DSH 0.2 Web)：Use npm for a normal installation. To develop the plugin, clone the repository,
build it locally, and invoke the matching CLI so an older global
`dsh` binary cannot install it into the wrong profile contract:

```sh
git clone --branch main --single-branch https://github.com/sluminositys/dsh-nested-followups.git
cd dsh-nested-followups
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm run check

dsh-nested-followups README · Build from source (optional, DSH 0.2 Web)：This creates a `link:` installation to the checkout. After pulling an update,
run `corepack pnpm run check` again and restart the web profile.

dsh-nested-followups README · Build from source (optional, DSH 0.2 Web)：**If installation fails:** a direct `git+https://...` install runs this package's
`prepare` script, which pnpm requires you to approve. Install npm `0.2.3`, or clone/build/link using
the commands above instead; the plugin never changes your script allowlist.
An error saying npm `0.2.2` is incompatible with DSH `0.2.x` refers to the old
npm artifact: install `0.2.3` explicitly instead.

dsh-nested-followups README · Official Desktop：Desktop uses the same Web UI, so the plugin does not need a separate canvas or
an Electron extension. Its plugins belong to the **`desktop` profile**, not
`web`; installing into one does not enable it in the other.

1. Launch a supported DSH Desktop version once. Use **Manage dsh Command… → Install**
   in its application menu to install the bundled CLI.
2. **Fully quit Desktop** (closing its window may only hide it).
3. Run the following command using Desktop's bundled `dsh`:

dsh-nested-followups README · Official Desktop：```sh
   dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-nested-followups@0.2.3
   ```

4. Reopen Desktop and select **Tree View** in a conversation. For a built local
   checkout, substitute `.` for the package name and run from that checkout.

dsh-nested-followups README · Official Desktop：Do not use npm's `dsh` or `pnpm dlx` for the `desktop` profile: only the bundled
command can manage it. Existing global installations can shadow that command;
check `dsh --version` and your shell's command path first. npm installation in
Desktop uses its bundled runtime; only source builds need separate Node and pnpm.
See the [official Desktop instructions](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5/apps/desktop/README.md#bundled-command-runtime).

dsh-nested-followups README · Why not a new chat or a sidebar thread?：| Approach | Relevant earlier context | Main stays clean | Can keep branching at later depths | Trail stays attached |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ask in the main chat | Yes | No | No | Not applicable |
| Open a new conversation | Lost or copied manually | Yes | No | No |
| Typical temporary sidebar Q&A | Varies | Usually | Usually a linear side thread | Usually not |
| **dsh-nested-followups** | **Exact ancestor path** | **Yes** | **Yes—recursively, with no fixed depth** | **Yes** |

dsh-nested-followups README · Why not a new chat or a sidebar thread?：The distinguishing feature is not the canvas. It is that any answer at any
depth can become another isolated fork point, and the same rule keeps applying
to every descendant. The tree is only the map that keeps those recursive
detours visible and attached to the root session.

_The diagram draws two nested levels and then an ellipsis: the same fork action
remains available on every answer at every later depth._

text:
dsh-nested-followups README · Use it：1. Chat normally. The standard DSH chat, sidebar, composer, and message
   rendering remain unchanged.
2. Select **Tree View**, choose an earlier completed assistant answer, and
   select **Ask follow-up**. The question grows to the right in a new branch.
3. On the latest answer in a branch, use **Continue this branch** to add the
   next turn downward. Use **Ask follow-up** to create another isolated branch
   to the right. Repeat **Ask follow-up** on any descendant answer to keep
   nesting as deeply as needed.
4. Return to **Chat** whenever you want to continue the main task. Its history
   contains no branch messages.

dsh-nested-followups README · Use it：| Action | Direction | Session effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Ask follow-up** | Right | Creates a new isolated child session at the selected answer |
| **Continue this branch** | Down | Adds the next exchange to the current branch session |

**Continue this branch** appears only on the latest completed answer in a
branch. Main-line nodes never offer it, so the two operations cannot be
confused.

dsh-nested-followups README · Why every level is a real branch：This is not a prompt that asks the model to pretend later messages do not
exist, and it is not a line drawn between unrelated chats.
section: Why every level is a real branch

text:
dsh-nested-followups README · Why every level is a real branch：- Every branch, including a branch created inside another branch, is a real
  DeepSeek Harness session with durable history.
- The same fork rule applies recursively at every level; the plugin does not
  impose a nesting-depth limit.
- Its seed is the exact ancestor path through the selected completed answer,
  using the same event-boundary semantics as DSH's session fork path.
- Later messages from the main task, parent side trail, and sibling branches are
  absent unless they are ancestors of the new branch point.
- Messages never flow upward to a parent session or sideways to a sibling.
- Branch tools are enforced read-only when they execute, protecting the shared
  workspace from side-question activity.
- The request prefix remains byte-for-byte compatible with the parent at the
  fork point, so the model provider can reuse its prefix cache.
section: Why every level is a real branch

text:
dsh-nested-followups README · What Tree View includes：- One card per user message and assistant answer, with the main conversation
  running downward and isolated branches growing to the right.
- Unlimited nested follow-ups and linear continuation within each branch.
- Search that reveals collapsed ancestors before centering a match.
- Focus mode, pan, zoom, fit-to-view, and a minimap for large trees.
- Progressive dot → capsule → card expansion, plus one-action collapse.
- Cascading branch deletion with an exact branch and message count.
- Durable branch metadata and per-conversation view state across restarts.
- No branch entries in the normal sidebar session list.

dsh-nested-followups README · Progressive collapse：A tree opens fully folded on first visit: the main conversation plus one dot
per answer that has branches. Select **⊕** to reveal one capsule per branch,
then select a capsule to restore that branch's cards. Child anchors stay folded
until you open them, so one expansion never floods the canvas with every
descendant.

dsh-nested-followups README · Progressive collapse：Alt-select **⊕** or a capsule to expand all descendants. **Collapse all**
returns top-level groups to dots. A pulsing blue marker means a folded
descendant is generating; red means one failed. The layout is restored per
conversation after a restart.

dsh-nested-followups README · Read-only branch execution：Branches share the main conversation's working directory, so allowing a side
question to write would be unsafe. The plugin therefore checks tools when they
actually run. Read operations are permitted; writes and unknown tools are
refused by default.

dsh-nested-followups README · Read-only branch execution：Allowed tools are `read`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep`, `lsp`, the `session_*`
query tools, `job_list`, `job_output`, `terminal_list`, `terminal_read`,
`list_agents`, and `get_goal`. Code Mode's `run_code` remains available because
every tool it invokes is checked individually.

dsh-nested-followups README · Provider prefix-cache reuse：A branch joins the same preset as its parent and does not rewrite tool
definitions, prompt sections, or presentation format. Its request therefore
starts with the same bytes as the parent request at the branch point. Providers
that cache request prefixes can reuse that context instead of reading the
inherited conversation again.

dsh-nested-followups README · Requirements：| Requirement | Version |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.1-rc.5`, plus the verified alpha and legacy host versions above |
| Node.js (source build / Web) | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |
| Package manager (source build) | pnpm |

dsh-nested-followups README · Compatibility notes：The source branch bridges both legacy rc and current 0.2 contracts: Session
snapshots, inherited history, read-only persistence handles, process-local
assistant streaming, tool results, native icons, and message rendering. It
does not patch DSH or rewrite its logs. Forks still stop at completed turns;
the newer host's ability to fork an open turn is deliberately not used.

dsh-nested-followups README · Compatibility notes：Automated validation and the exact runtime checks are recorded separately.
Desktop shares the Web plugin mechanism; a Web boot is not a packaged Desktop
end-to-end test.
See [DSH version compatibility](docs/dsh-version-compatibility.md) for the
contract mapping and maintainer verification procedure.

dsh-nested-followups README · Compatibility notes：The current development target is DSH `0.2.1-rc.5`; the same source is also
checked against `0.2.1-alpha.1`, `0.2.2-alpha.2`, and legacy `0.1.1-rc.2`.
These adapters are included in npm `0.2.3`. DSH `0.2.2-alpha.2` requires
Node.js 24.9 or later; packaged Desktop supplies its own runtime.

dsh-nested-followups README · Compatibility notes：**Branches cannot be continued from the standard chat view.** DSH currently
rejects user messages sent from the normal chat UI to a subagent-origin
session. Reading and continuing a branch therefore happen in Tree View. The
plugin probes for a future host capability that could safely restore native
continuation, but enables it only when DSH explicitly guarantees message
delivery.

dsh-nested-followups README · Compatibility notes：**Branches may appear in the built-in Subagent menu as disabled diagnostic
rows.** They cannot be selected, are skipped by keyboard navigation, and do not
count as active child agents. This does not affect the root conversation or the
sidebar, where branch sessions remain hidden.

dsh-nested-followups README · Uninstall：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-nested-followups
```

Uninstalling removes the plugin UI and services. It does not modify the main
conversation or delete persisted branch history.
